facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis
treated with fingolimod for 3 years
tender nodule on her forehead, which had gradually grown over 3 weeks
bumping her forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
denied fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia
Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
No other lesions on full-body skin examination
White blood cell count: 3.9/μL
Lymphocyte count: 0.65/μL
Skin biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation composed of histiocytes, giant cells, and lymphocytes admixed with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules
Tissue culture: Grew Cryptococcus neoformans
HIV test: Negative
A 62-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis
treated with fingolimod for 3 years
tender nodule on her forehead, which had gradually grown over 3 weeks
bumping her forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
denied fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia
Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
No other lesions on full-body skin examination
White blood cell count: 3.9/μL
Lymphocyte count: 0.65/μL
Skin biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation composed of histiocytes, giant cells, and lymphocytes admixed with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules
Tissue culture: Grew Cryptococcus neoformans
HIV test: Negative

concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules, and tissue culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans, which is diagnostic of Cryptococcosis.

The patient presented with a tender nodule on her forehead, which was found to be an eroded, crusted papule, and skin biopsy and tissue culture confirmed the presence of Cryptococcus neoformans, indicating Cutaneous Cryptococcosis.

The patient was treated with fingolimod for multiple sclerosis, which can cause immunosuppression, and presented with low white blood cell and lymphocyte counts, increasing her risk for opportunistic infections like Cryptococcosis.

rationales.F02: Fingolimod treatment increases the risk of opportunistic infections like Cryptococcosis.
rationales.F10: Skin biopsy showing granulomatous inflammation and narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules is diagnostic of Cryptococcosis.
rationales.F11: Tissue culture growing Cryptococcus neoformans confirms the diagnosis of Cryptococcosis.
rationales.F12: Negative HIV test reduces the likelihood of Immunodeficiency-associated Cryptococcosis.
